core_obligations: Reduce to a decreasing sequence of dense open sets by replacing U_n with the finite intersections U_1 cap ... cap U_n, and fix a nested fundamental system M_n of neighbourhoods of zero (proof lines 9046-9051).

Fix a point x and a neighbourhood M_k of zero, and construct y_1 in U_1 with y_1 in x + M_k, then k_1 > k with y_1 + M_{k_1} inside U_1, then y_2 in U_2 with y_2 in y_1 + M_{k_1}, then k_2 > k_1 with y_2 + M_{k_2} inside U_2, and continue inductively (proof lines 9056-9067).
Use completeness of M to form the limit y of the sequence y_i and note that x - y lies in M_k by construction (proof lines 9067-9069).
Show that y - y_i lies in M_{k_i} by writing the tail as a telescoping sum, hence y lies in y_i + M_{k_i} which is contained in U_i for every i, so the intersection is dense (proof lines 9069-9074).

The nearest records are 1744 (8696-8848, tag 07E5, Noetherian local algebras over characteristic-p fields) and 343 (9256-9320, tag 07NJ, continuous lifting through closed topologically nilpotent ideals); both are algebraicity statements about rings, not a completeness argument about a topological abelian group.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the Baire category theorem in the form this chapter needs: for a linearly topologized complete abelian group with a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of zero, a countable intersection of open dense subsets is dense (statement lines 9037-9042). The proof is a full 31-line construction (proof lines 9045-9075): after replacing the U_n by their finite intersections it builds, for a prescribed point x and a prescribed neighbourhood M_k of zero, a sequence y_i with y_i in U_i and y_i - y_{i-1} in M_{k_{i-1}}, where the indices k_i are chosen increasing so that y_i + M_{k_i} sits inside U_i, then uses completeness to produce the limit y and shows x - y is in M_k and y is in every U_i. The two places where the topology is really consumed are the choice of each k_i, which needs openness of U_i, and the passage to the limit, which needs completeness of M; the proof closes with the telescoping identity for y - y_i, so no step is left as routine.
